_meta.purpose: Offline prompt-injection fixtures (Decision 76). Each fixture is a synthetic data-room document with a planted injection, ingested through the real ingestion path next to the offline harness's clean Northwind data room (tests/fixtures/pipeline_harness.py). tests/test_injection_fixtures.py checks deterministic properties only: what the ingest screen flags, how the injection reaches the synthesis prompt (delimited, labelled, forged markers neutralised, content kept), and what the verifier and the validator report when a compromised model repeats the injected figure. No LLM is called: the model's reply is the scripted `compromised_answer`.
_meta.not_a_robustness_claim: These fixtures pin structural behaviour. They say nothing about whether a real model obeys an injection, and an adaptive attacker who reads injection_screen.py can word an injection the screen does not flag (arXiv 2510.09023). The delimiting and the verifier's figure checks do not depend on the screen.

fields.format: txt (document.text is the file), pdf_white_text (document.visible lines in black, document.hidden lines in white on a white page), xlsx_cell (document.rows on one sheet), txt_tag_characters (document.text plus document.hidden_ascii encoded as invisible Unicode tag characters)
fields.expect_signals: injection_screen signals the ingest screen must report for the document
fields.prompt_must_contain: strings the synthesis prompt must still show (the injection is kept as data, never dropped)
fields.prompt_must_not_contain: raw forms that must not reach the prompt
fields.compromised_answer: what a model that obeyed the injection would write; null when the fixture only checks ingest and prompt
fields.injected_figure: the figure only the injected text states
fields.expect_tainted: true when the injected figure sits in a flagged sentence, so the validator must name it; false when the injection only flags the passage (the answer is then downgraded because it cites a flagged passage)
